tasks.title: One seat-failure classifier, every caller migrated
tasks.intent: Every failed seat call is classified by one function, `classifySeatFailure`, into authoritative, account (balance/billing/quota/auth), rate-limited (with resetAt), transient or other, with provenance rules for tail sources. All current callers route through it and the by-hand checks are deleted, so an opencode `provider.quota: Insufficient Balance` result maps to the `usage-limit` outcome on the first attempt.
exclusions: Do not add phrases to `HALT_SIGNATURES` or change its groups.
Do not let a tail source (`stderr-tail`, `stdout-tail`) match `billing`, `payment required` or any account phrase outside `HALT_SIGNATURES`.
Do not change the recovery builders or the halt copy.
Do not add new outcome codes; map onto `usage-limit` and `unauthenticated`.
steps: Create `src/engine/runners/seat-failure.ts` exporting `classifySeatFailure(input: { message, code?, status?, providerType?, outcome?, source })`, `source` in `'result-error' | 'thrown' | 'stderr-tail' | 'stdout-tail'`. Results: `{ class: 'authoritative' }`, `{ class: 'account', cause: 'balance' | 'billing' | 'quota' | 'auth' }`, `{ class: 'rate-limited', resetAt }`, `{ class: 'transient' }`, `{ class: 'other' }`. Precedence authoritative -> account -> rate-limited -> transient -> other.
Authoritative outcomes: `user-abort`, `implementer-left-isolation`, `checkout-changed`, `implementer-recipe-invalid`, `input-too-large`, `missing-model`, `no-progress-cut`.

Account: status 402 (balance), 401/403 (auth); phrases `insufficient balance`, `insufficient credits`, `credit balance is too low`, `payment required`, `billing_hard_limit`, `billing_not_active`, `out of credits`, `account suspended`; `providerType === 'provider.quota'` with no parseable reset; auth phrases (`HALT_SIGNATURES.auth`, `unauthenticated`, `sign in`, 403 spellings). An account phrase outranks a 429 in the same text.
Tail sources match only `HALT_SIGNATURES` phrases; the broader account phrases live in `seat-failure.ts` and apply only to `result-error` and `thrown`.

Rate-limited: a limit phrase or 429 whose reset `parseUsageLimitReset` reads. Transient: the current `isTransientSeatFailure` rule unchanged. A bare 429 without status and without `hasUsageLimitNounCorroboration` is `other`.

Migrate callers: `runnerCallOutcome` (`call-result.ts`); the thrown-error branch in `implementers/pipeline/run.ts` (replace the `usageLimitDetailFromError` and `isAuthFailureError || isAuthFailureDiagnostic` branch with one classifier call, `source: 'thrown'`, status from `err.data.status ?? err.data.statusCode`); `haltFailure`/`namesHalt` in `process-invoke.ts`; `diagnosePlannerCallFailure`; `seatResetWaitDeadline`; `isTransientSeatFailure` becomes the classifier's transient arm.

Delete `usageLimitDetailFromError`; stop exporting `isAuthFailureDiagnostic`/`isAuthFailureError` to other modules. Keep `parseUsageLimitReset`, `usageLimitAdvice`, `runnerLoginInstruction`, `hasUsageLimitNounCorroboration`.

`seat-failure.test.ts`: a table of envelopes labelled `captured` or `synthetic` (opencode Go limit 429 and DeepSeek balance, codex usage limit and refresh-token, claude-code session/weekly/Opus limits, `Request rejected (429)`, `Credit balance is too low`, `Invalid API key · Please run /login`, antigravity `Individual quota reached … Resets in 2h6m30s` on stderr, command-code weekly limit and `Not authenticated`, Anthropic `rate_limit_error`, OpenAI `insufficient_quota`, Gemini `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, DeepSeek 402 `Insufficient Balance`) plus precedence rows.

tasks.title: State and action vocabulary for seat down
tasks.intent: The workflow state and recovery vocabulary can express a seat-down park, an automatic switch intent, a switch record and a later retry: `retry-later` is a recovery action labelled `Retry at <clock>` that seat-down halts allow; `interruptedStep.source` accepts `'seat'`; `pendingRecovery.switchSeat.auto` and `state.seatSwitches` parse; `RESTART_ATTEMPT_ON_SEAT` clears the pending recovery while keeping the attempt, the in-progress task and the interrupted step. Old state files still load.
exclusions: Do not add a new recovery reason.
Do not change how `RESET_TASK` behaves.
Do not wire `retry-later` application into the engine here; only the vocabulary and label.
steps: Add `retry-later` to `RECOVERY_ACTIONS` (`src/core/schemas/enums.ts`); `action-label.ts` spells it `Retry at <clock>` from the issue's `resetAt` with the existing reset formatter.

`SEAT_DOWN_ACTIONS` in `halt.ts`: `switch-seat`, `retry-later`, `retry-same-worker`, `skip-current-task`, `end-run`; the recovery policy under `src/core/schemas/recovery/` admits `retry-later` for seat-down halts.

`WorkflowStateSchema` gains optional `seatSwitches: { seat, from, to, cause, auto, configRevision, ts }[]`; `interruptedStep.source` gains `'seat'`; `SwitchSeatOfferSchema` gains optional `auto: { candidate, configRevision }`.

Add `RESTART_ATTEMPT_ON_SEAT { taskId }` (types.ts, machine.ts): clears `pendingRecovery`, keeps the task's `attempt` and `in_progress`, keeps `interruptedStep`, no lineage counter change. Add an action that appends one `seatSwitches` record.
Schema test: an old `state.json` without the new fields loads.

tasks.title: Declared fallback in seat config, kept by every writer and shown in Settings
tasks.intent: Each seat block accepts an optional `fallback: { tool, model, effort?, variant? }` validated through the seat's own schema as a cli runner; the config writers and the seat swap keep it; it is not part of the seat identity; Settings shows one read-only `fallback <identity>` line under each crew row that declares one.
exclusions: Do not add a default fallback, and do not change `init`.
Do not add a fallback editor to the picker or Settings.
Do not include `fallback` in the seat identity string.
steps: `createRunnerConfigSchema` and `createPlannerConfigSchema` accept optional `fallback`, validated as `{ kind: 'cli', ...fallback }` through the seat's schema; an unhostable tool fails with a message naming `fallback`; `effort` on a tool whose effort channel is `variant` fails.
`buildRunnerConfig`, the picker commit in `config-transforms.ts`, and `configWithSwitchedSeat` keep the seat's existing `fallback`.
`seatIdentitiesFromConfig` ignores `fallback`.
`deriveCrewRows` carries the fallback identity (`formatSeatCandidateIdentity`, axis word included); `row-view.tsx`/`format.ts` render one dim line `fallback <identity>`.
With no `reviewer:` block, the review seat uses `planner.fallback`.

tasks.title: Adapters pass observed status, provider type and the raw error line
tasks.intent: A failed call carries the provider's observed HTTP status and error type when the tool printed them, and the `runner_call_error` event carries the first raw error line, so the classifier reads `provider.quota` and 402/429 directly; copilot error lines become failed results. The captured DeepSeek envelope replayed through opencode's protocol events classifies as account/balance.
exclusions: No adapter invents a status or provider type it did not observe.
Do not change claude-code, cursor, command-code or antigravity parsing.
steps: `RunnerCallErrorSchema` gains optional integer `status` and bounded string `providerType`; `createRunnerCallRecorder` keeps them redacted and bounded like `message`.

`errorLineProtocolEvents` (final-group.ts, used by opencode and kilo) reads `error.status` or `error.data.statusCode` and `error.type` or `error.name`. Fixtures: `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"provider.quota","message":"Insufficient Balance (request_id: 021cfcdf-…)"}}` and the Go-limit envelope with `status: 429`.
`codexTurnFailedDetail` keeps a nested `error.type` as `providerType`.
`copilot.ts`: a `type: 'error'` line, or a result with `is_error` or a non-success subtype, becomes a failed result `{ code: 'copilot-error', message }`.
`runner_call_error` gains `rawTail`: the first error line, at most 2 KiB, redacted.
`runnerCallOutcome` and process-invoke pass `status` and `providerType` into `classifySeatFailure`.

tasks.title: One seat-down halt builder and a fallback-first swap offer
tasks.intent: `buildSeatDownIssue` builds the seat-down halt for every seat and cause with the S11 copy and actions, replacing the usage-limit and unauthenticated builders, and the swap offer lists the seat's declared fallback first with its model and effort, allowing the same tool on another model and saying why a blocked fallback is not offered.
exclusions: Do not add a new recovery reason.
Touch the engine call sites only as far as needed to compile after the deletion.
steps: `buildSeatDownIssue({ seat, runner, classification, words, requestId?, resetAt?, fallback?, task?, phase, ... })` in builders/task.ts: reason `runner-unauthenticated` for auth, else `runner-usage-limit` with `facts.cause` in `balance|billing|quota|rate-limit`.

Copy: title `Seat down · <SEAT> · <tool>` (`recoveryHaltLabel`, `CREW_SEAT_LABELS`); line 1 the cause in plain words (`Balance spent on <Provider>`, `usage limit · resets <clock>` via `formatResetNote`, `signed out`); `details[0]` the provider words verbatim with the request id; line 3 `fallback: <identity>` (`formatSeatCandidateIdentity`) or `no fallback declared`; a sign-in cause keeps `runnerLoginInstruction`.

Actions: `switch-seat` when offered, `retry-later` only with `resetAt`, `retry-same-worker`, `skip-current-task` only when the halt names a task, `end-run`. Recommended: `switch-seat` when offered, else `retry-later` with a reset, else `retry-same-worker`.

Route usage and auth cases of `buildPlannerCallFailedRecoveryIssue`/`diagnosePlannerCallFailure` to `buildSeatDownIssue`; delete `buildRunnerUsageLimitRecoveryIssue` and `buildRunnerUnauthenticatedRecoveryIssue` and move their tests.
`switchSeatOffer` excludes the current identity (tool and model), not the current tool, and passes `effort` and `variant` through.

`loadSeatSwapContext` takes the seat's `fallback` and puts it first when the remembered snapshot has its tool `ready` or `unverified`; `not installed`, `incompatible`, `unauthenticated`, `unavailable` block it with one detail row naming why.
`runnerHaltRow` leads with the cause words and the provider quote, spelling the reset once from `resetAt`.

tasks.title: Every seat halts as seat down at once and parks the cut brief
tasks.intent: An account or unrecoverable rate-limit failure on any seat (first build attempt, local retries, consult, planning, final review, triage) raises the seat-down halt on the attempt it failed, with 0 retries and 0 consults. A cut brief keeps its workspace, is parked with `source: 'seat'`, and its attempt is not counted. When the halted seat declares a usable fallback with no earlier automatic switch in this run, the halt carries `switchSeat.auto = { candidate, configRevision }`.
exclusions: Do not apply the switch here; only raise the halt with its intent.
Do not change attempt or consult bounds; no refunds.
steps: `implementation-failure.ts`: one `buildSeatDownIssue` path for `unauthenticated` and `usage-limit` outcomes; no `workspace.cleanup()` on it; dispatch `INTERRUPT_STEP { step: { kind: 'brief', taskId, attempt }, source: 'seat', cut: 'mid-step' }` with the halt.
`run-implementation.ts` retains the workspace for a seat-down failure as for a resumable stop (`isResumableWorkspaceStop`).
`escalation/handle.ts`: `unauthenticatedHalt` and `usageLimitHalt` become one `seatDownHalt`; `runLocalRetries` checks `haltsLocalRetries` before `COUNT_ATTEMPT`.
`planning/failure.ts`, `task/retry.ts` (consult), `final-review.ts` (`seat-blocked`; no `reviewer:` targets the plan seat and `planner.fallback`) and `triage.ts` use `buildSeatDownIssue`.

Set the auto intent only when the class is account (or rate-limited past `BOUNDS.rateLimitResetWaitMs`), the halted seat declares `fallback`, the offer contains it, and `state.seatSwitches` has no `auto` entry for that seat; `configRevision` is the revision read at the halt.
Tests: an opencode balance result on attempt 1 halts with 0 retries and 0 consults and the provider's words; a seat with an `auto` entry gets no auto intent.

tasks.title: Retry later waits for the reset the user chose; a far reset halts
tasks.intent: Taking `retry-later` on a seat-down halt resolves the recovery and sets the seat wait to the reset, so the next continue waits until then and re-runs the step; the run reads as stopped and the byline says `Waiting for <tool> · resets <clock>`. A codex reviewer 429 with a 2-minute reset waits and the review runs again and passes; with a reset outside `BOUNDS.rateLimitResetWaitMs` the reviewer halts as Seat down with `Retry at <clock>` offered.
exclusions: Do not offer `retry-later` without a known reset.
steps: `actions.ts` applies `retry-later`: resolve the recovery and dispatch `SET_SEAT_WAIT { seat, resetAt }`; no wait bound.
`resumeSeatWait` (`run/init.ts`) honours it (fake-clock test).
`StopReason` in `run-status.ts` reports a waiting seat as stopped; `openRunByline` reads `Waiting for <tool> · resets <clock>`.

`final-review-seat-wait.test.ts`: (a) a codex reviewer 429 with a 2-minute reset publishes `seat_wait_started`, then the review runs again and passes; (b) a codex reviewer 429 whose reset lies beyond `BOUNDS.rateLimitResetWaitMs` raises a seat-down halt on the review seat whose actions include `retry-later`, labelled `Retry at <clock>`.

tasks.title: The switch commits once: prepare, one-seat config write, state record
tasks.intent: Applying a seat switch prepares the switched config first, then writes only that seat into `config.yaml` against the revision read at the halt, then resolves the recovery with `RESTART_ATTEMPT_ON_SEAT`, appends `state.seatSwitches` and publishes `seat_switched` (one transcript row). Stop, conflict and crash cases leave a consistent run, and `continue --action switch-seat:` uses the same one-seat writer. A scripted run with a spent implementer and a declared fallback switches, keeps the partial file and the attempt number, and completes.
exclusions: Never rewrite seats other than the switched one.
Do not resolve the recovery before the config write is saved.
steps: Add `recordSeatOfRecord(projectDir, seat, runner, expectedRevision)` in `src/core/config/load/record-seat.ts`: patch one seat block (or the failing implementer profile) through `transactConfigDocument`. Delete `recordSeatsOfRecord` from the continue command and call the new function.

Reorder `switchSeatAndPrepareResume`: (1) prepare on the switched config, no writes; (2) only when `prepared` and not aborted, `recordSeatOfRecord`, rechecking the abort inside the transaction; `conflict` keeps the halt pending with one warning row `config changed meanwhile · the halt stays`; (3) on `saved`, `transitionAndSave` resolves the recovery, dispatches `RESTART_ATTEMPT_ON_SEAT` for a halt naming a brief (else re-issue the step as today), appends `seatSwitches`, publishes `seat_switched`.

Re-entry after a crash between 2 and 3: seat of record equal to the candidate -> step 3 without a second write, `auto: true`; different -> drop the intent, resolve onto the seat of record, `auto: false`.
A stop during steps 1-2 writes nothing and leaves the halt pending with its intent.
Add the `seat_switched` event and one transcript row `BUILD → <identity> · <cause words>`.

Integration test: a scripted `agent` implementer writes a partial file then emits the balance line at attempt 1 with a declared fallback -> `seat_switched`, partial file survives, `attempt` unchanged, the continued attempt counts once, the run completes; a second seat-down on the switched seat halts without auto intent; crash injection, manual change, abort and conflict cases.

tasks.title: TUI driver takes the automatic switch and opens the picker on the fallback
tasks.intent: In the TUI, a seat-down halt with an `auto` intent switches without opening the picker; a halt without it opens the seat picker on the first candidate's tool row with its model and effort drafted, and Escape returns to the panel unchanged. Boundary seat-change requests are kept per seat, so the swap never discards another seat's change, and a newer manual change to the same seat wins.
exclusions: Do not fork a per-role picker.
Do not add a fallback editor to the picker.
steps: `createRecoveryDriver` routes an `auto` candidate straight to `applyOfferedSeatSwap`.
`pickSwappedSeat` opens the overlay with `toolRowFocus(tool)` plus the candidate's model and effort drafted in the picker's `OptionAxisName` state.

`requestSeatChangeAtBoundary`/`consumeSeatChange` hold a per-seat set `{ seat, configRevision }`; the swap consumes only its own seat's entry and only when its revision is not newer than the one it wrote.
Tests: auto skips the picker; another seat's boundary change survives; a newer same-seat change wins; Ink test for the drafted picker and Escape.

tasks.title: Headless seat-down policy and record
tasks.intent: Headless `start` and `continue` follow `--on-seat-down halt|switch`: with a declared fallback they switch automatically (before the run and after each return) under the run's signal handlers; otherwise they exit 1 with a `recovery_required` record that names the halt, cause, provider words, request id, reset, fallback and a resume line with `@<effort>`. No picker opens headlessly.
exclusions: An automatic switch does not change the exit code rules.
steps: Add `--on-seat-down <halt|switch>` in `src/cli/options.ts` and on `start` and `continue`; default `switch` when the halted seat declares a fallback, else `halt`; explicit `halt` overrides any intent; explicit `switch` with no fallback anywhere exits 2 naming `fallback`.

`runHeadless` installs SIGINT/SIGTERM before the preflight and applies an auto intent through `applyOfferedSeatSwap` before the run and after each `runWorkflow` return, in a loop; write a `seat_switched` record.

`recovery_required` gains `halt`, `cause`, `providerMessage`, `requestId`, `resetAt`, `fallback`; the resume line prints `switch-seat:<tool>:<model>@<effort>`; `parseSeatSpecOption` carries `@<effort>` into the candidate by the tool's effort channel.

tasks.title: doctor --probe-seat captures one raw call
tasks.intent: `splitbrief doctor --probe-seat <plan|build|review>` sends `Reply with the word ok.` through the seat's own adapter in an isolated workspace (60 s, 64 KiB), writes stdout, stderr, exit status and the classification, redacted, to `.splitbrief/probes/<tool>-<date>.jsonl`, and prints the class and first error line; plain `doctor` makes no call.
exclusions: Ordinary `doctor` stays read-only and unchanged.
steps: Register the option; its help text says it makes one paid call.
Reuse the raw capture in `contract-harness-raw.ts` and `classifySeatFailure`.
Tests: a scripted tool writes the probe file with the class; without the flag no call is made.

tasks.title: Skills learn the account rule and retry later
tasks.intent: The generated skill blocks state that an account refusal halts at once and a declared fallback switches the seat, list the `retry-later` row, and `wait-attempt.sh` takes its phrase list from `HALT_SIGNATURES`; the four skills are regenerated and in sync.
exclusions: Do not hand-edit generated skill blocks; regenerate them.
steps: `seatRecovery()` gains the account rule and the `retry-later` row.
Generate the `wait-attempt.sh` phrase list from `HALT_SIGNATURES`, then regenerate the skill copies under `skills/` with the sync script.

tasks.title: Gallery scenarios show seat down, the fallback and the switched seat
tasks.intent: The visual gallery renders the seat-down panels with a fallback in the fixture config, a new `workflow-seat-switched` scenario with the transcript row and the new header seat, the Settings fallback line, and a sessions row for a seat-down run.
exclusions: Do not run the screenshot tool; SPLITBRIEF collects the renders.
steps: `workflow-recovery-usage-limit`, `workflow-recovery-plan-seat`, `workflow-recovery-review-seat`, `workflow-at-rest-halted` fixtures use `buildSeatDownIssue` output and a config with a fallback.
Add `workflow-seat-switched` to `testing/visual/catalog.ts`.
`overlay-settings*` fixtures include a fallback; `sessions` includes a seat-down row.
Fixture projections reference no deleted builder.

tasks.title: Deleted-symbol invariant gate and docs for seat down, fallback, switch, headless policy and probe
tasks.intent: A new invariant gate in `scripts/check-invariants.ts` fails when any file under `src/` contains `buildRunnerUsageLimitRecoveryIssue`, `buildRunnerUnauthenticatedRecoveryIssue`, `usageLimitDetailFromError` or `recordSeatsOfRecord`, and passes on the migrated tree. The canonical docs, CHANGELOG and CLAUDE.md describe the classifier and its classes, the one Seat down section with the builder, `retry-later`, the declared fallback, the automatic switch with its commit sequence and resume rules, the headless flag, the probe and the gaps of prose-only tools.
exclusions: Do not edit any file under `.nuke/`.
Write in ASD-STE100 style, matching the surrounding docs.
Do not document behaviour the code does not have.
steps: Add one gate to `scripts/check-invariants.ts`, in the style of the existing gates, that scans `src/` for the four deleted symbol names and fails naming each file and symbol it finds; list the gate in `docs/INVARIANTS.md`.

`APPROVAL-AND-RECOVERY.md`: "Seat trouble" (classifier), one "Seat down" section, reason table rows, headless paragraph, gaps list (copilot, cursor, kilo, opencode sign-out, stderr-only balance text), first-attempt halt site `task/implementation-failure.ts`.
